prior_issues.description: Update method sends an empty Healthcheck struct with only modified fields — the Cloudflare API may interpret zero-value fields (Interval=0, Timeout=0, Retries=0, Suspended=false) as intentional updates rather than 'unchanged'. This is a potential correctness issue depending on the API behavior, though the current implementation matches the pattern used in other services in this project.

Get method unconditionally wraps errors as notFound — not all API errors are 404s (could be auth failure, network error, rate limit). Other services in this project have the same pattern, so it's consistent but semantically imprecise.

Missing CheckRegions, HTTPConfig, and TCPConfig from cloudflare.Healthcheck — the Healthcheck struct omits fields that users may need for HTTP-specific checks (expected status codes, headers, method) and TCP config, and for selecting check regions. These are important for non-trivial healthcheck setups.

Get() wraps all API errors as notFound — a 403 or 500 from Cloudflare would be misclassified as R2NotFoundError. Other services in the project have the same pattern so this is consistent, but still semantically wrong.

Missing CheckRegions, HTTPConfig, and TCPConfig fields from cloudflare.Healthcheck — the Healthcheck struct omits these fields that exist in the upstream type, which means users cannot configure check regions or protocol-specific settings (HTTP headers, method, expected codes, follow redirects; TCP method). This limits the usefulness of the library for non-trivial healthcheck configurations.
Get() and Update()'s fetch-error path wrap all API errors as notFound — a 403 or 500 is misclassified. Consistent with other services in the project but semantically imprecise.
Missing CheckRegions, HTTPConfig, and TCPConfig fields from cloudflare.Healthcheck limits non-trivial healthcheck setups (HTTP-specific settings, TCP config, region selection).

CheckHTTP creates a new http.Client per call instead of reusing d.httpClient — the redirect-tracking closure is the reason, but it means timeout and transport settings from the constructor are partially wasted (timeout is re-applied, but any custom transport would not be)

CheckSSL uses tls.DialWithDialer which does not respect the ctx cancellation — context is accepted but only the timeout from d.timeout is honored; a long-running TLS handshake won't cancel on ctx.Done()

queryResolver silently swallows individual DNS lookup errors (LookupHost, LookupMX, LookupNS) — if LookupHost fails but MX succeeds, the error from LookupHost is lost entirely rather than being surfaced in a warnings field
NewDomainService receives nil for DNS and SSL services — if GetDetail internally calls methods on those without nil-checking, it will panic rather than return an error

Update command `--enabled` flag defaults to `true` (line 322). Running `cosmoflare email rules update ZONE RULE --name=X` silently re-enables a disabled rule. `--priority` defaults to 0, silently resetting priority. These defaults are appropriate for create but dangerous for update — consider using `cmd.Flags().Changed("enabled")` to detect whether the user explicitly set the flag.

Update command sends `emailPriority=0` and `emailEnabled=true` to `svc.UpdateRule` even when user only intended a partial update (e.g., just changing the name). The Cloudflare API treats this as a full replacement, so unset fields overwrite current values.

`TestNewEmailService_EmptyAccountID` (line 35 of email_test.go) doesn't actually test the empty-accountID validation path — the nil-API check fires first. The comment acknowledges this but the test name is misleading and the accountID validation in `NewEmailService` is effectively untested.

`EmailDestination.Verified` uses `time.Time` with `json:"verified,omitempty"` but `omitempty` is a no-op on `time.Time` structs in Go — zero time still serializes as `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Use `*time.Time` to match the pattern in `EmailSettings` for consistent omission of unset dates.

Update command `--enabled` flag defaults to `true` (line 322). Running `cosmoflare email rules update ZONE RULE --name=X` silently re-enables a disabled rule. `--priority` defaults to 0, silently resetting priority. The fix is to use `cmd.Flags().Changed("enabled")` / `cmd.Flags().Changed("priority")` to detect explicit user intent, and make `UpdateRule` accept pointer types (`*int`, `*bool`) for optional fields.

UpdateRule API signature uses concrete `priority int, enabled bool` — it always sends these values to Cloudflare even when the user only intended a partial update. The Cloudflare API treats UpdateEmailRoutingRule as a full replacement, so unset fields overwrite current values. The library layer needs optional-field semantics (pointer types or an options struct).

`TestNewEmailService_EmptyAccountID` (line 32 of email_test.go) passes nil API client AND empty accountID — the nil check fires first, so the accountID validation path is never exercised via `NewEmailService`. The comment acknowledges this but the test name is misleading. Should pass a non-nil API to test the accountID check, or rename the test.

`EmailDestination.Verified` uses `time.Time` with `json:"verified,omitempty"` but `omitempty` is a no-op on `time.Time` structs in Go stdlib encoding/json (zero time still serializes as `"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"`). Use `*time.Time` to match the pattern in `EmailSettings` for consistent zero-value omission.

Update command `--enabled` defaults to `true` (line 322 of cmd/email.go). Running `cosmoflare email rules update ZONE RULE --name=X` silently re-enables a disabled rule. `--priority` defaults to 0, silently resetting priority. Use `cmd.Flags().Changed("enabled")` and `cmd.Flags().Changed("priority")` to distinguish explicit from default values.

UpdateRule service method signature takes concrete `priority int, enabled bool` — there is no way for the CLI to signal 'user did not set this field'. The Cloudflare API treats the update as a full replacement, so unset fields overwrite current values with defaults. The service layer needs `*int`/`*bool` or an opts struct to support partial updates.

`TestNewEmailService_EmptyAccountID` (line 31-36 of email_test.go) passes nil API + empty accountID — the nil-API check fires first, so the empty-accountID validation path is never exercised through `NewEmailService`. The comment acknowledges this but the test name is misleading and the code path is effectively untested via this constructor.

`EmailDestination.Verified` uses `time.Time` with `json:"verified,omitempty"` (line 38 of email.go) — `omitempty` is a no-op on `time.Time` structs in Go. Zero time serializes as `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` rather than being omitted. Use `*time.Time` to match the pattern in `EmailSettings` for consistent behavior.

Update command `--enabled` flag defaults to `true` (line ~322 of cmd/email.go). Running `cosmoflare email rules update ZONE RULE --name=X` silently re-enables a disabled rule. `--priority` defaults to 0, silently resetting priority. Must use `cmd.Flags().Changed("enabled")` and `cmd.Flags().Changed("priority")` to detect explicit user intent before passing to UpdateRule.

UpdateRule function signature takes `priority int, enabled bool` as concrete types — impossible to distinguish 'user set false/0' from 'user didn't set'. The Cloudflare API treats this as full replacement, so unset fields overwrite current values. Needs pointer types or an options struct to support partial updates.

`EmailDestination.Verified` uses `time.Time` with `json:"verified,omitempty"` but `omitempty` is a no-op on `time.Time` in Go — zero time serializes as `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Should use `*time.Time` to match the pattern in `EmailSettings` for consistent JSON output.
`TestNewEmailService_EmptyAccountID` passes nil API client, so nil-API check fires first. The accountID validation path in `NewEmailService` is effectively untested — the test name is misleading.

Update command leaks sentinel value: `priority = -1` is passed directly to `svc.UpdateRule` which sends it to the Cloudflare API as the actual priority. The comment says 'sentinel: UpdateRule should preserve existing' but the service layer has no sentinel-detection or fetch-before-update logic — it passes -1 verbatim to `cloudflare.UpdateEmailRoutingRuleParameters.Priority`.

Update command's `enabled` handling is broken: when `--enabled` is not explicitly set, `enabled = true` is sent to the API. The comment claims 'preserve enabled state via fetch-before-update in service layer' but no such fetch exists in `EmailService.UpdateRule`. Running `update ZONE RULE --name=X` on a disabled rule silently re-enables it.

Update command sends empty matchers/actions to the API when user doesn't specify `--match-to`/`--match-all`/`--forward-to`/`--drop`. The service layer builds empty `cfMatchers`/`cfActions` slices and passes them to the API, which likely treats this as a full replacement — wiping existing rule configuration.

TestNewEmailService_EmptyZoneID passes nil as the API client (`NewEmailService(nil, "", "acct123")`), so the nil-API check fires before the empty-zoneID check. The test passes for the wrong reason. The test for EmptyAccountID is correctly structured (passes a real client).

Update command partial-update is broken: the service layer `UpdateRule` unconditionally passes `priority` and `enabled` to Cloudflare's API (which is a PUT/full-replace). When user runs `cosmoflare email rules update ZONE RULE --name=X`, the cmd layer sends priority=-1 (sentinel) and enabled=true directly to the API — there is no fetch-before-update in the service layer despite the comment claiming one exists (line 593). This will corrupt rule state.

Empty matchers/actions on update silently clear the rule: when user only changes `--name` without specifying `--match-to` or `--forward-to`, nil matchers/actions are passed to the service layer which builds empty `cfMatchers`/`cfActions` slices and sends them to Cloudflare's UpdateEmailRoutingRule — a full replacement that wipes the rule's routing configuration.
TestNewEmailService_EmptyZoneID passes nil API, so the nil-API check fires first — the test passes but doesn't actually validate the empty-zoneID path. Test name is misleading.

The `--enabled` flag on the update command defaults to `true` via `BoolVar` (line 322 in init). Even with the `cmd.Flags().Changed` guard, the comment says 'preserve enabled state via fetch-before-update in service layer' but no such logic exists — this is a false comment that masks the bug.

Update command sends priority=-1 sentinel directly to Cloudflare API when user omits --priority. The sentinel is assigned in cmd/email.go (~line 580) but UpdateRule in pkg/r2go2/email.go passes it through to cloudflare.UpdateEmailRoutingRuleParameters.Priority unchanged — no service-layer handling exists despite the comment claiming otherwise.

Update command sends empty matchers/actions slices when user only wants a partial update (e.g. --name only). In runEmailRulesUpdate, if neither --match-to nor --match-all is set, matchers stays nil → make([]..., 0, 0) → empty array sent to API. Cloudflare treats this as a full replacement, wiping the rule's existing matchers and actions.

The cmd.Flags().Changed('enabled') guard in runEmailRulesUpdate sets enabled=true when the flag is unchanged — the comment says 'preserve enabled state via fetch-before-update in service layer' but no fetch-before-update exists in EmailService.UpdateRule. Running 'cosmoflare email rules update ZONE RULE --name=X' silently re-enables a disabled rule.

EmailService.UpdateRule signature takes (priority int, enabled bool) — value types with no sentinel/nil representation. The service layer cannot distinguish 'user set priority=0' from 'user didn't set priority'. Needs *int/*bool or a separate options struct to support true partial updates.
Update command partial-update logic is broken: `priority = -1` sentinel is never interpreted by service layer's `UpdateRule` — Cloudflare receives literal -1 as priority value

When `--enabled` flag is not explicitly set, `enabled = true` is still sent to Cloudflare API (comment claims 'fetch-before-update in service layer' but no such logic exists in `UpdateRule`), silently re-enabling disabled rules
When neither `--match-to` nor `--match-all` is set on update, empty `matchers` slice is sent to Cloudflare which may clear existing matchers (full replacement semantics)
Same issue for `actions` — partial update with only `--name` sends empty matchers+actions, potentially destroying the rule configuration

The .review.json lists 4 blocking issues from round 7, but commits 4f1053b and 732af9d address all of them: EmailDestination.Verified is *time.Time, update handler uses cmd.Flags().Changed() for partial updates, and the EmptyAccountID test now passes a valid cf client to reach the accountID check. The .review.json metadata is stale relative to the final code state.
Tests pass nil as context (e.g. svc.GetRule(nil, "")) which works because validation short-circuits, but is not idiomatic — context.Background() would be safer if validation order ever changes.
